How ZIPs Were Selected

Georgia ZIPs compared with the current list

Every Georgia ZIP was compared with the 8 current ZIPs with the highest close rates: Hampton 30228, Griffin 30223, Griffin 30224, McDonough 30252, McDonough 30253, Locust Grove 30248, Jonesboro 30238, Stockbridge 30281. Close rates are from the 10/12 email.
Traits compared
Home value and household incomeShare of homes $300K–$750KOwner-occupied shareShare of homes built 2000 or laterHousing densityNumber of owner-occupied homesMiles from the Hampton office
509 ZIPs were compared after removing ZIPs with fewer than 500 owner-occupied homes. 125 match the profile as closely as 90% of the current list's good-fit ZIPs. Wave 1 is the 52 closest matches, which take the list to 100 ZIPs. Wave 2 is the other 73.
45 of 52 Wave 1 ZIPs have at least 30% of homes from $300K to $750K.

Add the 52 Wave 1 ZIPs to the GA Home and Auto ListGOAL
We will add Wave 1 to the shared ZIP list once approved. The list goes from 48 to 100 ZIPs.
Metric behind it: households in the footprint go from 429,636 (10.5% of GA) to 1,028,454 (25.2%).
2
Confirm the 9 Wave 1 ZIPs Beyond 57.3 MilesAgency
Flowery Branch 30542, Centerville 31028, Oakwood 30566, Cartersville 30120, Cartersville 30121, Gainesville 30504, Athens 30607, Gainesville 30507, Bonaire 31005 sit farther from the office than any current ZIP. Wave 2 ZIPs can replace any that are left out.
Metric behind it: 43 of 52 Wave 1 ZIPs are within 57.3 mi.
3
Confirm Three Details Before LaunchAgency
Whether Allstate restricts writing in any of the 21 Wave 1 counties. Whether the 10/12 close rates cover GOAL leads or the full book. Whether the Home value range of $300K to $700K stays as is.
Metric behind it: 3 of the 8 highest-closing ZIPs (Griffin 30223, Griffin 30224, Jonesboro 30238) have under 30% of homes from $300K to $750K.

Metric behind it: both waves cover 1,724,892 households (42.3% of GA).
